I farm this the way I have done for years, but I do adjust a little when I see what works around me. In Quzhou, if I want steady wheat and maize on 10.1 mu, I cannot be stingy with fertilizer, especially nitrogen, because one bad harvest costs more than a few extra bags. I have middle school education, so I do look at the balance a bit, not just throw on urea. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer in the ground, and then topdress when the wheat starts pushing hard in spring. Wheat here drinks water at the key stages, so with my well I will not let it go dry. For maize after wheat, I will still spend on hybrid seed because the stand is better and the ears are more reliable. Maize grows fast in summer, so I will keep nitrogen strong, give phosphorus and potassium with the base, and irrigate if the rain misses. I will do close to what has worked in my own field and what the better growers nearby do: not the cheapest way, but the safer way for yield.
